reuse.why: Fintegra linking reuses linkBankSyncAccount and findOrCreateBank, but the local unlink re-implements unlinkAccount's field reset and the Fintegra download/balance code copies the Akahu versions instead of sharing them.

duplication.why: downloadFintegraTransactions is a verbatim copy of downloadAkahuTransactions, the fintegra starting-balance branch copies the akahu branch, the unlink field reset copies unlinkAccount, and the same guard call is repeated in six provider functions.

placement.why: The guard lives in accounts/app.ts but is called from every provider wrapper rather than inside the shared linkBankSyncAccount, and the closed-account rule and the take-over mutation are tucked into a function named as a duplicate-link assertion.

scope.why: Changes track the four steps; the client edits are minimal type-driven additions and release notes are conventional.

maintainability.why: An 'assert' helper that also mutates other accounts and checks closed status, called separately by each provider, plus copy-pasted provider code, means every new provider or rule must be wired in several places.

bypasses_abstraction.where: accounts/app.ts assertBankAccountNotLinked resets link fields itself instead of reusing unlinkAccount's logic; the guard sits outside linkBankSyncAccount, the shared link path.

disguised_duplication.where: The copies (Fintegra download vs Akahu download, fintegra vs akahu balance branch, unlink field reset) are near-verbatim, not disguised.

abstraction_drift.where: assertBankAccountNotLinked in accounts/app.ts gains the replaceExistingLink parameter, a closed-account branch and a replace-and-unlink branch; all six provider link functions call it, none skip it.
